usable: Jinja-style separation of data from presentation as a design goal

not_creditable: S20 reconcile_ok/idempotent/backup flags are observed evidence

S18/S20 PEN floats have an authorized money-boundary contract

roadmap_expectation.T1: Templates: Jinja y separación datos/presentación; condiciones, tablas y formato seguro
roadmap_expectation.T2: DOCX/PDF: estilos y secciones; extracción de PDF digital y detección de imagen/OCR
roadmap_expectation.T3: Informe: resumen ejecutivo, método y hallazgos; gráficos, tablas, fuentes y limitaciones
roadmap_expectation.T4: QA: redacción, accesibilidad y consistencia; render visual, provenance y aprobación
roadmap_expectation.gate: Accessible Insights Dashboard & Reporting Factory genera dashboard, DOCX/PDF y workbook desde una corrida, con números reconciliados y revisión visual

live_site.evidence: Public page exposes Section 21 'Reportes trazables' and the canonical tagline. The text fetch does not expose the hydrated S21 lesson body, so rendered-only defects remain unresolved rather than invented.

runtime_validation.environment: Python runtime with jinja2, python-docx, reportlab, pypdf and PyMuPDF available
checks: T1-B current formatter raises TypeError when median=None, contradicting the promised em-dash missing path
default Jinja Undefined renders a missing variable as an empty string while StrictUndefined raises UndefinedError
DOCX current example reopens; actual styles are Title, Heading 1 and Normal, but the published theory check never inspects style names
A white-on-white PDF can have extractable n=40 text and a non-empty rendered PNG, proving non-empty render bytes do not establish visual legibility
ReportLab default Helvetica successfully round-trips 'sintético' through pypdf in the current runtime, so stripping the accent is not required for this demo
rounding [28.04, 28.0, 28] to one decimal yields [28.0, 28.0, 28.0], reproducing the published false-green consistency check

findings.evidence: Opening and T3-B require DOCX/PDF to share totals and n with S18-S20, but the campaign ledger marks S18-S20 REPAIR_REQUIRED and specifically rejects S20 reconciliation/provenance flags as trusted.
findings.impact: A polished report can launder an upstream false-green metric into an apparently audited executive artifact.
findings.repair: Require one validated upstream payload identity and re-run the critical reconciliation at the S21 boundary before rendering any document.

findings.evidence: The gate says one run generates dashboard, workbook, DOCX/PDF with reconciled numbers, but the eight theory snippets are isolated fixtures with separately hardcoded values and no orchestrating run.
findings.impact: The central CP-N2-B integration claim is never demonstrated; all local examples can pass while cross-artifact drift remains possible.
findings.repair: Add one closure harness that loads the validated payload once, renders all artifacts, reopens them, reconciles canonical records, hashes outputs and leaves pending_review.

findings.evidence: Opening says one source makes disagreement 'imposible en vez de improbable'.
findings.impact: A shared source reduces drift but renderers, formatting, stale artifacts, manual edits and code defects can still produce disagreement.
findings.repair: Say a single canonical payload plus post-render reconciliation makes disagreement detectable and blocks publication.

findings.evidence: T1-A promises a versioned context with run_id/metrics/limits reused across artifacts; s21_th_1 passes three ad-hoc keyword arguments and contains no run_id, version or reusable context object.
findings.impact: The learner sees presentation separation but not the provenance contract the outcome actually requires.
findings.repair: Build and validate a context object with schema_version, run_id, payload_id, canonical metric records and limits, then reuse it in at least two renderers.

findings.evidence: T1-A tells a serious factory to configure StrictUndefined, but both theory Jinja environments use the default Undefined behavior. Current Jinja renders a missing variable as an empty string by default.
findings.impact: A missing n/source/limit can disappear silently from an executive document instead of failing closed.
findings.repair: Use Environment(undefined=StrictUndefined, ...) in the canonical factory environment and demonstrate a missing required key raising before publication.

findings.evidence: Opening frames escaping as if direct field insertion generically breaks 'the document', while Jinja autoescape is specifically an HTML/XML escaping policy and the course also creates DOCX via python-docx and plain text/Markdown.
findings.impact: Learners may equate HTML escaping with universal sanitization or document safety.
findings.repair: Teach sink-specific encoding: HTML autoescape for HTML, library-managed OOXML text for python-docx, and explicit plain-text/Markdown character policy; never call one escape mechanism universal sanitization.

findings.evidence: Opening says the same em dash represents both a missing value and a value that exists but must not be shown.
findings.impact: Missingness and redaction have different semantics, audit implications and denominator treatment; one glyph makes them indistinguishable to the reader.
findings.repair: Keep status metadata and visibly distinguish '— (sin dato)' from 'REDACTADO' or another explicit policy-approved marker.

findings.evidence: T1-B promises None -> —, but s21_th_2 always executes '%.2f'|format(r.median). In the current runtime median=None raises TypeError: must be real number, not NoneType.
findings.impact: The canonical example does not implement one of the subtopic's main safety rules.
findings.repair: Branch before formatting or centralize format_metric(value, status, precision) so None returns an explicit missing token and numeric values follow the canonical display policy.

findings.evidence: T1-A says KPIs arrive already rounded from Python, while T1-B explicitly formats 28.456 to 28.46 in Jinja and T4-A allows one decimal in summaries versus two in detail.
findings.impact: The learner cannot tell whether the canonical payload stores full-precision values, rounded publication values or display strings.
findings.repair: Define three layers: canonical numeric value, publication/quantization rule if business-required, and channel display precision. Formatting may change the string but must not be used to prove source-value equality.

findings.evidence: Learning outcome and prose require extraction of real Heading styles, yet s21_th_3 only checks text substrings and PK signature. It never inspects p.style.name or heading order after reopening.
findings.impact: A document with bold Normal paragraphs can satisfy the published theory check while failing the semantic outline contract.
findings.repair: After reopening, assert the expected Title/Heading levels and logical order, and test table headers/alt properties where the report contains those elements.

findings.evidence: PDF examples import fitz. Current PyMuPDF documentation recommends import pymupdf; the legacy fitz name can collide with an unrelated PyPI package named fitz.
findings.impact: A fresh learner environment can fail for a dependency-name collision despite installing the documented pymupdf package.
findings.repair: Use import pymupdf and pymupdf.open(...); if fitz is mentioned, label it as legacy compatibility only.

findings.evidence: T2-B says PNG render proves visual legibility; code only checks png.exists() and size > 0. A white-on-white text PDF reproduced both extractable n=40 and a non-empty PNG while the text was visually invisible.
findings.impact: The visual QA gate can be green on an unreadable page.
findings.repair: Call rendering a surface for review, not proof. Record actual human/visual-harness review of clipping, contrast, font rendering, pagination and figure/table placement.

findings.evidence: T2-B prose promises an image-only PDF negative case and needs_ocr, but s21_th_4 generates only a digital text PDF and never computes or prints needs_ocr.
findings.impact: The learner never practices the abstention branch that is the core distinction of the subtopic.
findings.repair: Create a synthetic image-only PDF fixture, show extract_text empty/insufficient, set needs_ocr=true and prohibit downstream factual extraction until OCR is explicitly performed and reviewed.

findings.evidence: S21 claims accessible reporting, but the ReportLab canvas example only draws text and tests extraction/render. It does not establish tagged headings, reading order, document language, table structure or image alternatives for the PDF.
findings.impact: A searchable PDF can still be inaccessible to assistive technology.
findings.repair: Either generate/test a tagged accessible PDF path or explicitly state that the simple ReportLab canvas PDF is a visual/digital artifact whose accessibility is not established; require PDF accessibility checks before the CP-N2-B gate.

findings.evidence: T3-A describes pack_report validation requiring n, unit and H->evidence and says decision=None, but s21_th_5 is only a hardcoded dict with no validator and no decision field.
findings.impact: An eloquent but untraceable finding can pass the example because the promised acceptance rules are not executable.
findings.repair: Implement validate_report(report) that checks required sections, canonical metric references, n/unit, evidence IDs, limits and explicit decision=None/pending-human-decision state.

findings.evidence: T3-B claims checksum/parity across PNG, XLSX and DOCX and shared run_id, but s21_th_6 opens none of those artifacts. It asserts only that the character string '40' appears in a caption and prints an in-memory metrics dict.
findings.impact: The central closure control can never detect an Excel/DOCX/dashboard disagreement.
findings.repair: Extract canonical records from each generated artifact and compare key, metric, numeric value, denominator, filter/universe, display precision and run_id; fail closed on any mismatch.

findings.evidence: s21_th_7 rounds [28.04, 28.0, 28] to one decimal, obtains [28.0, 28.0, 28.0], and declares consistente=True.
findings.impact: Different underlying channel values can be hidden by display rounding, exactly the discrepancy S21 claims to prevent.
findings.repair: First compare canonical numeric values/metric IDs before formatting; separately test that equal canonical values produce the same display string under the declared presentation profile.

findings.evidence: T4-A normalizes monetary values with round(float(v), precision), while S02 explicitly established Decimal for soles and warned against converting money back to float.
findings.impact: The report boundary reintroduces the numerical representation defect the early curriculum told the learner to avoid.
findings.repair: Carry Decimal or integer cents into the publication context; use explicit quantization/formatting policy without round(float(...)) for PEN.

findings.evidence: T4-A says alt text must mention n and unit, but its example is 'Barras mediana por región, n por barra en tooltip': it contains neither an actual n nor PEN and delegates information to a tooltip unavailable in a static document.
findings.impact: The learner can copy an alt string that fails the exact accessibility rule being taught.
findings.repair: Use a concrete equivalent such as 'Ticket mediano por región en la muestra web: Lima 28.0 PEN (n=40), ...' or point to an adjacent accessible table containing all values.

findings.evidence: T4-A reduces the minimum to has_h1 plus at least one alt longer than 10 characters; theory code implements neither. It omits logical heading order, actual alt attachment, simple table/header semantics and document accessibility inspection.
findings.impact: A document can satisfy length/heading-presence heuristics while remaining inaccessible.
findings.repair: Define observable DOCX/PDF accessibility checks aligned to the artifact: logical heading hierarchy, actual alternative text on visuals, simple header-marked tables, language/reading order where supported, and a documented accessibility review.

findings.evidence: s21_th_8 hardcodes {'dashboard':'ok','xlsx':'ok','doc':'ok'}, hashes the literal bytes b'synthetic', and computes no artifact hash despite prose requiring hashes of artifacts and visual checklist evidence.
findings.impact: The manifest can assert a healthy package without observing any package file.
findings.repair: Derive status from executed checks and compute SHA-256 for the validated input payload, template/source artifacts and each actual output file.

findings.evidence: T4-B specifies ready(checklist)=all(dashboard,xlsx,doc), a pending_review manifest on disk and human actor/timestamp workflow; s21_th_8 has no checklist function, no visual review fields and only prints JSON to stdout.
findings.impact: The package can appear complete without a persisted reviewable state transition or evidence of human inspection.
findings.repair: Persist manifest.json atomically with checklist results, artifact identities and pending_review; only a later human review action may add reviewer/timestamp and transition to approved/rejected.

findings.evidence: Opening callout says ReportLab/Helvetica demos intentionally write 'sintetico' ASCII. In the current runtime, ReportLab default Helvetica and pypdf round-trip 'sintético' correctly.
findings.impact: The course lowers Spanish redaction quality for a workaround not demonstrated to be necessary in the supported stack.
findings.repair: Write correct es-PE text with accents; if a font limitation is ever real, teach font embedding/Unicode support explicitly instead of normalizing Spanish to ASCII.

findings.evidence: CASO-LIM-021 repeatedly compares Lima and Madrid as region peers without defining a multinational universe, continuing the geography ambiguity already flagged in S19-S20.
findings.impact: Population/coverage language becomes incoherent and weakens the course's Peru-grounded business scenario.
findings.repair: Use a coherent Peru fixture (for example Lima/Arequipa/Trujillo) or explicitly rename the dimension to market/city and define the multinational universe.

findings.evidence: Dense use of context, factory, provenance, missing, caption, bundle, outline, a11y, pending_review and other English terms appears faster than stable Spanish-first definitions.
findings.impact: Unnecessary lexical switching increases extraneous cognitive load in a course whose stated language is Peruvian Spanish.
findings.repair: Introduce Spanish concept first and preserve API/status literals only where they are actual code contracts, e.g. contexto, factoría/generador de reportes, trazabilidad/procedencia, dato faltante, pie de figura, paquete, esquema, accesibilidad.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Using Template(...) is always a security defect.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The first theory template is plain text. The real defect is sink-specific policy plus failure to use StrictUndefined; the separate HTML example correctly demonstrates explicit autoescape.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: An empty pypdf extraction proves the PDF was scanned.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: PDF text extraction can fail for digitally-born content too. needs_ocr is acceptable as a workflow flag for unavailable/insufficient text, but should not be presented as perfect document-origin classification.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: PK signature alone is the only DOCX validation.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The example also reopens the file with python-docx, which is materially stronger. The confirmed defect is that the promised semantic style checks are absent.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: round(28.04, 1) is numerically wrong Python behavior.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The result is expected. The defect is using display-normalized equality as evidence that upstream canonical values agree.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Legacy import fitz is universally broken.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: It remains a compatibility alias and works in many environments. It is P2 because current PyMuPDF recommends pymupdf and documents a real collision risk with the unrelated fitz package.

external_validation.result: Current official Jinja docs recommend explicit Environment configuration, document that autoescape is not a universal default, and expose the undefined policy hook used for StrictUndefined.
pypdf documentation distinguishes digitally-born, scanned and OCRed PDFs and states pypdf is not OCR; extractability alone is not a complete document-origin/accessibility test.
Current PyMuPDF docs recommend import pymupdf and warn that legacy import fitz can collide with an unrelated PyPI package.

Microsoft accessibility guidance requires logical built-in headings, alt text and simple tables with header information; W3C PDF techniques include tagged headings, reading order, table markup, alt text and document language.

priority_order: P1-1: repair F02/F16/F17/F21/F22 so a single run actually derives and reconciles artifact evidence rather than fabricating green states
P1-2: repair F05/F08/F10/F12/F13/F15 so each subtopic's executable example proves the contract its prose states
P1-3: repair F14/F19/F20 to prevent searchable/visible documents from being mislabeled accessible
P1-4: repair F01/F18 so uncertain upstream metrics and PEN float do not become polished report facts
P1-5: repair F04/F07 context provenance and missing/redaction semantics
P2: then repair F03/F06/F09/F11/F23/F24/F25 redaction, scope, import and terminology issues

USABLE: data/presentation separation as a design objective
HTML autoescape must be explicit and |safe/Markup disable escaping
DOCX should use semantic heading styles rather than visual bold alone
PDF text extraction and rendering answer different questions
publication requires human review rather than script auto-approval
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: em dash can mean both missing and redacted
rounding different numbers to one display value proves parity
float rounding is acceptable for PEN
alt length >10 plus any H1 proves document accessibility
S22_watchlist: S22 must consume a persisted pending_review manifest derived from actual S21 files, not a printed dict.
No email draft may treat S21 artifact statuses or hashes as trustworthy until S21 derives them from executed checks.
Recipient-facing numbers must bind to canonical metric IDs/denominators before display formatting.
Human approval must have actor/timestamp and may not be inferred from factory completion.
Accessibility/provenance defects remain open and must not be erased by email packaging.
